req.title: PUT is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall produce the same terminal state when PUT is repeated with an identical payload for the same playerId.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that the PUT operation should be idempotent, meaning that repeated requests with the same payload should result in the same state and response. This is crucial for ensuring consistency in RESTful APIs. The tests are designed to verify this behavior by checking the response status and the state of the resource after repeated PUT requests.

tests.name: test_put_idempotency_positive
preconditions: Player with squad number 5 exists in the database.
actions: Send a PUT request to update the player with squad number 5.
Send the same PUT request again.
expected: Both requests return HTTP 204 No Content.
Player data remains unchanged after the second request.
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app)

player_data = {
    "firstName": "Vivaan",
    "middleName": "",
    "lastName": "Nair",
    "dateOfBirth": "1905-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "squadNumber": 5,
    "position": "Central Midfield",
    "abbrPosition": "AM",
    "team": "Independiente",
    "league": "Liga Profesional",
    "starting11": False
}

response1 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/5", json=player_data)
assert response1.status_code == 204

response2 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/5", json=player_data)
assert response2.status_code == 204

tests.name: test_put_idempotency_negative
preconditions: Player with squad number 5 exists in the database.
actions: Send a PUT request with mismatched squad number in the path and body.

    "firstName": "Vivaan",
    "middleName": "",
    "lastName": "Nair",

    "squadNumber": 6,
    "position": "Central Midfield",
    "abbrPosition": "AM",
    "team": "Independiente",
